unit.explanation: One patient had PDOTS testing for lenvatinib, tislelizumab, and their combination, then received the matched lenvatinib-plus-tislelizumab regimen.

platform.explanation: Biopsy fragments were embedded in collagen and cultured in a 3D microfluidic PDOTS chip.

readout.explanation: AO/PI fluorescence was used to quantify relative cell viability and derive the Organoid Killing Index.

direction.explanation: OKI equals 1 minus relative viability, so greater killing/lower viability indicates greater sensitivity.

threshold_rule.explanation: A predefined cutoff classified OKI greater than 40% as sensitive.

threshold_timing.explanation: The article describes OKI > 40% as a pre-defined sensitivity criterion.

patient_mapping.explanation: The assay, treatment, and follow-up outcomes are traceable to one identified 64-year-old male patient.

regimen_match.explanation: The clinically administered lenvatinib-plus-tislelizumab regimen was the combination tested in PDOTS.

n_units.explanation: The report contains a single patient-regimen observation, not a validation cohort.

split.explanation: No training/test split or cohort-level predictive evaluation was performed in this single-case proof-of-concept report.

headline.blocked_reason: No global clinical or toxicity predictive headline is reported; the study describes concordance in only one patient and explicitly states that this is preliminary proof-of-concept rather than definitive validation.

notes: PDOTS OKI values were 31% for lenvatinib, 25% for tislelizumab, and 50% for the combination.
The patient achieved a partial response after six cycles and maintained it for 14 cycles.
The cited 88% predictive accuracy concerns prior NSCLC work and is not a headline computed from this article's HCC evidence.
